Split into 2 children. One reuses the comparator-accepted declaration dpf_pushforward_formula_boundaryVanishes, whose frozen type is byte-identical. The other is one new lemma, dimred_mbl_pfb_c1_compact_perturbation.

WHY SPLIT. Steps 0 and 3–6 of the supplied proof are Simon 6.2.24(1) for a C¹ map: mollify, show the pulled-back forms are test forms, use naturality of d and ∂X = 0, then pass to the limit. That argument is already formalized and accepted in the DAG as dpf_pushforward_formula_boundaryVanishes (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_boundary-a1, candidate 74a1c6be, isolated comparator passed). Its accepted dependencies are dpf_smooth_approx_compact_perturbation, dpf_pb_smooth_pullback_isTestForm and dpf_pb_imrep_pullback_integral_tendsto. It covers C¹ maps that equal the identity off a compact subset of U. Re-proving it here would duplicate a long accepted formalization; without a split it cannot be used, because only listed prerequisites are available to the implementer.

The only other obligation is step 2's cut-off, a reusable C¹ lemma. A similar lemma, dtc_bc_lc_pf_c1_compact_perturbation, exists but cannot be used: it is unaccepted (rlcr-lean), and it does not record K' ⊆ O, which is needed to get K' ⊆ U. So the new lemma gets a fresh, globally unique name. The twin node dor_lmb_pc_pushforward_boundaryVanishes has the same type but is unaccepted, so it is not shared.

MAPPING OF SUPPLIED STEPS TO CHILDREN.
- Step 2 (cut off f near K) becomes c1_perturbation. The cut-off is taken relative to the identity, φ = χ·f + (1−χ)·id, instead of χ₁·f together with a second cutoff ζ. Applied to O ∩ U, it gives φ = id off a compact K' ⊆ O ∩ U ⊆ U, and φ = f, Dφ = Df on an open V ⊇ K.
- Steps 0 and 3–6 become perturbed_boundary (reused). Because φ = id off K' ⊆ U, the pull-backs ψ_k^#η by the smooth approximants are automatically test forms in U, supported in tsupport η ∪ K'. This does the job of ζ and of the locality step 5(b). Dominated convergence replaces the uniform estimate of 5(a).
- Step 1 (*), that only values on K matter because Hⁿ(M∖K) = 0, becomes step 2 of the parent assembly below.

PARENT ASSEMBLY (the supplied proof with these factors).
(1) Apply c1_perturbation to (O ∩ U, K, f). The hypotheses hold: O ∩ U is open (IsOpen.inter), K ⊆ O ∩ U, and f is C¹ on O ∩ U (ContDiffOn.mono). This gives φ, V, K' with:

  - K' compact with K' ⊆ O ∩ U ⊆ U;
  - φ C¹ on ℝ^P;
  - φ = f and Dφ = Df on V;
  - φ = id off K'.
(2) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The integrands θξ(ω(f x)∘Df(x)) and θξ(ω(φ x)∘Dφ(x)) agree at every x ∈ M ∩ K ⊆ V. The set {x ∈ M : x ∉ K} = M∖K is Hⁿ-null, so they agree Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. and the integrals coincide (setIntegral_congr_ae, R.measurableSet_carrier). Hence Q satisfies the push-forward formula with φ.
(3) Apply perturbed_boundary with U, K := K', T := X, S := Q, R and φ. Its hypotheses are: U open, R represents X, K' compact with K' ⊆ U, φ C¹, φ = id off K', the formula from (2), and BoundaryVanishes X. It returns BoundaryVanishes Q. The case n = 0 is handled inside the child.

subproblems.title: C¹ cut-off of f near K to a compact perturbation of the identity supported in O
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ O compact, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O; f is arbitrary off O). Then there exist a map φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^P (ContDiff ℝ 1 φ), an open set V ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ V, and a compact set K' with K' ⊆ O, such that φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for every x ∈ V (Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x), and φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (V K' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen V ∧ K ⊆ V ∧ IsCompact K' ∧ K' ⊆ O ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ (∀ x ∈ V, φ x = f x ∧ fderiv ℝ φ x = fderiv ℝ f x) ∧ ∀ x, x ∉ K' → φ x = x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (Cutoffs) of the parent proof, specialized. The parent cuts f off to g = χ₁·f with g = f near K. Here the cut-off is taken relative to the identity, φ = χ·f + (1 − χ)·id, so that in addition φ = id off a compact subset of O. The parent's conclusion "g(x) = f(x) and Dg(x) = Df(x) on a neighbourhood of K" is kept.
Notation: E := ℝ^P (Euclid P, a finite-dimensional and hence proper real normed space); thickening r K := {z : infEdist(z, K) < r}; cthickening r K := {z : infEdist(z, K) ≤ r}; Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x.
1. Margin. K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ O (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put s := thickening δ K (open, isOpen_thickening), t := cthickening (δ/2) K (closed, isClosed_cthickening) and V := thickening (δ/2) K (open, isOpen_thickening). Then K ⊆ V (self_subset_thickening, since δ/2 > 0), V ⊆ t (thickening_subset_cthickening), and t ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ and δ/2 < δ). If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the steps below go through unchanged.
2. Smooth cutoff. Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma in the finite-dimensional real space E (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, with smoothness order ⊤ : ℕ∞) to the open set s and the closed set t ⊆ s. It gives χ : E → ℝ, C^∞, with values in [0, 1], support χ = s, and χ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ t. In particular χ is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le), and χ = 1 on V ⊆ t.
3. The compact set K'. Let K' := tsupport χ = closure (support χ) = closure s. Then K' ⊆ cthickening δ K (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ O by step 1. K' is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and lies in the compact set cthickening δ K (IsCompact.cthickening, E proper), so K' is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
4. Definition. For x ∈ E put φ(x) := χ(x)·f(x) + (1 − χ(x))·x. No regularity of f off O is used.
5. φ = id off K'. If x ∉ K' = tsupport χ, then χ(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so φ(x) = 0·f(x) + 1·x = x.
6. φ = f near K. Let x ∈ V. Since V is open, it is a neighbourhood of x. Every y ∈ V lies in t, so χ(y) = 1 and φ(y) = 1·f(y) + 0·y = f(y). Thus φ and f agree on a neighbourhood of x (φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f). This gives φ(x) = f(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.eq_of_nhds) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq: the Fréchet derivative at x depends only on the germ at x).
7. φ is C¹ on E. By contDiff_iff_contDiffAt it suffices to show ContDiffAt ℝ 1 φ x for every x ∈ E.
 (a) x ∈ O. O is open, so O ∈ 𝓝 x and f is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). χ is C¹ at x by step 2, and the constant 1 and the identity are C¹. The product of a real C¹ function with a vector-valued C¹ map is C¹ at x, and so are sums and differences of C¹ maps (ContDiffAt.smul, ContDiffAt.add, ContDiffAt.sub). Hence φ = χ·f + (1 − χ)·id is C¹ at x.
 (b) x ∉ O. Then x ∉ K', because K' ⊆ O (step 3). The complement of the closed set K' is an open neighbourhood of x on which φ = id (step 5). So φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] id, and φ is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq with contDiffAt_id).
8. Conclusion. The triple (φ, V, K') has all required properties:
 - V is open and K ⊆ V (step 1);
 - K' is compact and K' ⊆ O (step 3);
 - φ is C¹ on E (step 7);
 - φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for every x ∈ V (step 6);
 - φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K' (step 5). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ O; V := thickening (δ/2) K is an open neighbourhood of K, contained in t := cthickening (δ/2) K ⊆ s := thickening δ K.
Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff): χ ∈ C^∞(E, [0,1]) with support χ = s and χ = 1 exactly on t; K' := tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ O is compact.
φ := χ·f + (1 − χ)·id equals id off K' and equals f on the open set V, hence φ = f and Dφ = Df on V (EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
φ is C¹ at points of O (C¹ combination of χ, f, id) and at points off O (φ = id near them, as K' ⊆ O), hence ContDiff ℝ 1 φ.

subproblems.title: Simon 6.2.24(1) for a C¹ compact perturbation of the identity: ∂T = 0 implies ∂S = 0 (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Let K ⊆ U be compact and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on ℝ^P with φ(x) = x for x ∉ K. Let S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a current with S(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Dφ(x) = fderiv ℝ φ x, Hⁿ = μHE[n], and β∘L := β.compContinuousLinearMap L. If ∂T = 0 (BoundaryVanishes T; vacuous for n = 0), then ∂S = 0 (BoundaryVanishes S).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (T S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ x, x ∉ K → φ x = x) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ φ x)) ∂μHE[n]) → BoundaryVanishes T → BoundaryVanishes S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(1) (∂f_#T = f_#∂T), extended from smooth to C¹ maps through 2.24(2) by approximating φ with smooth maps.
This is the audited proof of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dpf_pushforward_formula_boundaryVanishes (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_boundary-a1, candidate 74a1c6be), whose frozen type is reused verbatim. Its smooth-approximation step is the accepted declaration dpf_smooth_approx_compact_perturbation (candidate 6b000c36); it is written out here as step 2, so the argument is self-contained.
In the selected parent's proof this covers steps 0 and 3–6 (reduce to S(dη) = 0, mollify, pull back, use naturality of d and ∂T = 0, pass to the limit), for a C¹ map that is the identity off a compact subset of U.
Notation: E := ℝ^P; M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ := Hⁿ⌞M; λ := Lebesgue measure on E and ∗ convolution with respect to λ; I := identity of E. For a smooth map χ : E → E and a form α of degree d, χ^#α(x) := α(χ(x))∘Dχ(x); this equals SimonGMT pullbackFormWithin univ χ α, since fderivWithin on univ is fderiv (fderivWithin_univ). d := exteriorDerivative = extDeriv. ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) is the C^∞ condition.
1. Reduction. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes S is True by definition. Let n = m + 1 and assume T.boundary = 0. By extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) it suffices to prove S.boundary(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, S.boundary(η) = S(exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η), the test form whose underlying form is dη. Fix η ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
2. Smooth approximants. Claim: there are C^∞ maps ψ_k : E → E (k ∈ ℕ), a compact K' ⊆ U and C ∈ ℝ such that ψ_k = id off K', ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ C for all k and x (so C ≥ 0), and ψ_k(x) → φ(x), Dψ_k(x) → Dφ(x) for every x. Proof:
 (a) Margin. K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ > 0 with K' := cthickening δ K = {x : infEdist(x, K) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open; K' = ∅ if K = ∅). K' is compact (IsCompact.cthickening, E proper).
 (b) Perturbation. g := φ − id is C¹ and g = 0 off K. So Dg = Dφ − I vanishes on the open set E ∖ K (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Thus g and Dg are continuous with support in the compact set K, and A := sup_x ‖Dg(x)‖ < ∞.
 (c) Mollifiers. For k ∈ ℕ let β_k : ContDiffBump (0 : E) have 0 < rIn < rOut = δ/(k+2), and put ρ_k := β_k.normed λ. Then ρ_k is C^∞, ρ_k ≥ 0 (ContDiffBump.nonneg_normed), ∫ρ_k dλ = 1 (ContDiffBump.integral_normed), and ρ_k(y) = 0 for |y| ≥ δ/(k+2). Define ψ_k := id + ρ_k ∗ g, i.e. ψ_k(x) = x + ∫ρ_k(t) g(x − t) dt (the convolution ρ_k ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ, λ] g).
 (d) Smoothness. ρ_k is C^∞ with compact support and g is continuous, hence locally integrable. So ρ_k ∗ g is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with n = ⊤ : ℕ∞), and ψ_k is C^∞.
 (e) Support. Let x ∉ K'. If ρ_k(t) ≠ 0 then |t| < δ/(k+2) < δ, so x − t ∉ K: otherwise infEdist(x, K) ≤ |t| < δ and x ∈ K'. So g(x − t) = 0 whenever ρ_k(t) ≠ 0. Hence (ρ_k ∗ g)(x) = 0 and ψ_k(x) = x, for every k.
 (f) Derivative bound. g is C¹ with compact support and ρ_k is locally integrable, so D(ρ_k ∗ g)(x) = ∫ρ_k(t) Dg(x − t) dt (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right). So Dψ_k(x) = I + ∫ρ_k(t) Dg(x − t) dt. Using ρ_k ≥ 0 and ∫ρ_k = 1, ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ ‖I‖ + ∫ρ_k(t)‖Dg(x − t)‖ dt ≤ 1 + A =: C.
 (g) Pointwise convergence. Fix x. rOut(β_k) = δ/(k+2) → 0, and each h ∈ {g, Dg} is continuous, so |(ρ_k ∗ h)(x) − h(x)| ≤ sup_{|t| ≤ δ/(k+2)} |h(x − t) − h(x)| → 0 (ContDiffBump.convolution_tendsto_right_of_continuous). Hence ψ_k(x) → x + g(x) = φ(x) and Dψ_k(x) → I + Dg(x) = Dφ(x).
 For P = 0 the claim is trivial: E is a point, g = 0 and ψ_k = id = φ.
3. Pulled-back test forms. Let α ∈ {η, dη}; α is C^∞ with compact support in U (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm, tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset).
 Smoothness: ψ_k^#α(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Dψ_k(x))) (α(ψ_k(x))). Here x ↦ α(ψ_k(x)) is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp) and x ↦ Dψ_k(x) is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right). L ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM L is analytic on all of End(E) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiffOn with uniqueDiffOn_univ). Applying a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps to a C^∞ family of vectors is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply). So ψ_k^#α is C^∞.
 Support: let F₀ := tsupport α ∪ K', a compact subset of U. If x ∉ F₀, the open set W := E ∖ F₀ is a neighbourhood of x on which ψ_k = id. So Dψ_k = I on W, and ψ_k^#α(z) = α(z) = 0 for z ∈ W. Hence tsupport(ψ_k^#α) ⊆ F₀ ⊆ U and ψ_k^#α has compact support.
 Therefore ψ_k^#η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and ψ_k^#(dη) ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
4. Naturality of d. d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη) as forms on E. This is SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with domains univ (open), ψ_k C^∞ on univ, MapsTo univ univ and η smooth; it rests on Mathlib extDerivWithin_pullback. It is combined with the identifications exteriorDerivativeOn univ α = extDerivWithin α univ = extDeriv α = dα (Mathlib extDerivWithin_univ) and pullbackFormWithin univ ψ_k α = ψ_k^#α (Mathlib fderivWithin_univ). So exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m (ψ_k^#η) is the test form ψ_k^#(dη) (Subtype.ext).
5. The approximating values vanish. Since T.boundary = 0 and R represents T, for every k: 0 = T.boundary(ψ_k^#η) = T(d(ψ_k^#η)) = T(ψ_k^#(dη)) = R.action(ψ_k^#(dη)) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(dη(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x)) dHⁿ(x) =: I_k.
6. Dominated convergence. Put h_k(x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(dη(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x)) and h(x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(dη(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)).
 (a) Measurability: each h_k and h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. θ is measurable and ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. The covector fields x ↦ dη(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x) and x ↦ dη(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) are continuous, because dη, ψ_k, φ, Dψ_k and Dφ are continuous and (β, L) ↦ β∘L is jointly continuous (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM). Evaluation is continuous bilinear.
